versions.summary: Links each provider's current terms and explains how the gateway's, the serving provider's and your own key's terms apply to the route you choose.

Discloses the Experiential Labs promotional route for Free-plan chats, on which Experiential Labs captures prompts and responses by default, keeps them for up to 30 days and may use them to develop, evaluate and improve its services and hosted models.

Adds an optional marketing email choice, asked in a separate unticked box and withdrawable in Settings or on the data rights page; no marketing email is sent yet. Corrects where files are stored: new uploads and generated files are written to a private bucket, while profile pictures and files stored before that move can be opened by anyone who has their address, and a data export is downloaded through a short-lived link. MiniMax models receive nothing from Managed Cloud and are reachable only with your own key; Qwen and Zhipu requests go through OpenRouter unless AGI holds its own key for that provider. Says how a notice about an incident would reach you.

Adds how the Google connectors access, use, store and share Google user data, and states compliance with the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements. Product analytics now also covers usage events from the AGI apps recorded against your account, never your messages or files, so a consent given under an earlier version covers page views only, and a workspace administrator can turn analytics off for every member. Adds that a deleted conversation can be restored for 30 days before a daily job permanently deletes it, and that background jobs are kept for up to 30 days.

Adds the checks the referral program runs against self-referral, on the basis of legitimate interests: a one-way hash of the network you signed up from, and a comparison of your app installations, your card's Stripe fingerprint and your email address with those of the person who referred you. Updates the number of user-scoped tables account erasure covers.

Adds that on the Experiential Labs promotional route for Free-plan chats, Experiential Labs keeps prompts and responses for up to 30 days and may use them to develop, evaluate and improve its services and hosted models, and that its no-training setting does not stop this capture.

Adds how dictation and Voice Mode audio is handled: it goes to OpenAI and we keep none of it. Adds that a picture you attach has its location, camera and time details removed before it leaves your device, and is not sent if that cannot be done. Adds a security incidents section on the breach procedure, its 72-hour clock for notifying a regulator and how a notice would reach you, and says that some models are reached through an inference gateway, each named on the subprocessors page.
Appeals can be filed in the product or through the appeal form, each with a reference, as well as by email.
The website now starts on Skip approvals instead of asking before every tool action, and the policy describes the actions that still need your review.

Lists two new browser storage entries used only when you tick the marketing email box at sign-up: the privacy notice revision and a random identifier for that sign-up attempt. Explains Global Privacy Control in more detail: with the signal on, new optional choices such as marketing email and waitlist product updates are recorded as refusals and analytics stays off, while a marketing email choice already saved on your account stays until you withdraw it in Settings or the consent centre.

States that we now honour Global Privacy Control, which the policy said we did not read: a browser that sends it is treated as refusing analytics and the product-update list, over any choice stored earlier. Corrects where the identity provider's cookies come from, removes two browser storage entries the product no longer writes, and adds two it does: the account that dismissed the Free plan notice, and a momentary check that local storage works. A visitor who chose under an earlier version is asked to choose again.
Fly.io now also runs our malware scanner, which every uploaded file passes through and which keeps no copy.

Corrects the Experiential Labs entry against its current privacy and data-controls documents and adds its Free-plan promotional route, on which Experiential Labs captures prompts and responses by default, keeps them for up to 30 days and may use them to develop, evaluate and improve its services and hosted models.

Adds five recipients: the Cheaper Inference and Experiential Labs inference gateways, Cloudflare Workers AI, Vercel AI Gateway, and OpenAI for dictation and Voice Mode. Removes MiniMax, which was listed but received no Managed Cloud traffic, and corrects when Qwen and Zhipu requests pass through OpenRouter.

Restates how deletion works in narrower, verified terms: stored media is deleted before its catalogue record and retried if deletion fails, erasure reports list what was deleted, skipped or failed, and the scheduled purge erases account data before the sign-in identity and stops if erasure is incomplete.

Adds the signed-in refund request; a refund, once per account, of an unused plan payment or of unspent top-up credits asked for within 7 days; the 14-day withdrawal in the EU, EEA and UK, prorated by the credits used when you asked at checkout for immediate access; and the hold on your plan and credits while a payment dispute is open. Corrects how plan upgrades are billed: an upgrade starts a new billing period on the day you upgrade.
A referral trial that converts to a paid plan is billed every month; the earlier text also mentioned yearly billing, which the trial does not offer.

The first version of these terms: who can take part in the referral program, the friend's free trial, the bonus credits each of you can earn and when they expire, and the fair use checks against self-referral.
Adds the in-product Report an accessibility barrier ticket beside the email address.

Corrects three rows against the code: release signing covers the macOS desktop app only, as there is no Windows build; business continuity says the host-neutral restore drill runs every week and only the production database has no scheduled restore test; and security event logging adds the log of each call a connector makes. Records the 21 September review of the subprocessor list, re-measures row-level isolation and the protected route groups, and says /status runs its checks at most once a minute.
Adds product usage events, sent only in managed-cloud mode and only after you allow product analytics, as a data category, and removes the statement that no usage event leaves your device.

Corrects the EU AI Act disclosures for the planned app: it will tell you it is an AI system on a first-run screen you accept before its first model request, and only its planned on-device data export, not the per-conversation export sheet, will mark chat transcripts with a machine-readable AI-generated marker.
Adds the Impersonation section and an impersonation option on the report form.

Adds the optional marketing email choice at sign-up, which rests on your consent and can be turned off on its own. Clarifies that leaving that box unticked at sign-up records no decision, while the early-access forms record the boxes you leave unticked.

Adds connectors you sign in to at the provider. For those, AGI stores the access token and any refresh token encrypted in your account, together with the scopes granted and a label for the connected account. When you disconnect, or your account is deleted, AGI deletes its copy and asks the provider to revoke the tokens where it can; otherwise remove AGI in that provider account settings. Connectors whose provider registration is not in place are marked Needs setup and cannot be connected.
Attached files, project knowledge files and selected connector context now count as untrusted content, so a turn that holds them asks before anything could send data out.

A new website account now starts on Skip approvals instead of Ask before every action: eligible reads, searches, sandboxed code and reversible actions run without a prompt, while destructive or unknown actions, your saved per-tool choices and workspace restrictions still apply, and the server asks when your setting cannot be read.
